primary.title: HMSI to focus on dealer margins, buyer retention
primary.description: Mumbai: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) is prioritising dealer profitability and customer retention over pushing market share in the country's fiercely competitive two-wheeler market, with greater focus on expanding its vehicles in operation than chasing annual volume rankings."Share is just one year's result. Our business is not just one year," HMSI president and chief executive Tsutsumu Otani told ET. HMSI has been the country's second-largest two-wheeler maker since its separation from Hero MotoCorp in 2014, and even outsold its former partner in monthly sales on multiple occasions. During April-October FY27, HMSI's domestic dispatches stood at 3.7 million units, while Hero MotoCorp dispatched 4.0 million units.Also Read: Harley-Davidson to introduce new models under X range in India, expand dealership networkOtani said HMSI will focus on growing and maintaining its units in operation (UIO), or the number of Honda vehicles on Indian roads. "For the dealer network, the most important thing is units in operation, not share," he said. "Honda tries to maintain units in operation. That means maintaining and protecting our dealer network, profitability and business."The strategy marks a shift in emphasis from the pursuit of market leadership to building a sustainable customer base in a market where competition has intensified across commuter motorcycles, scooters and premium bikes.Also Read: Bullet on a budget? 'Dug-Dug' Royal Enfield may get into classic hunt for India's next million bikersThe focus on customer retention and repeat purchases comes as HMSI looks to tap growth across segments. The company sees considerable headroom in the motorcycle market, which Otani estimates at 23-24 million units annually. He also sees greater participation of women in personal mobility as an opportunity to expand the scooter market. Women currently account for only 10% of HMSI's business. A change in this mix could open up a new avenue of growth for the company, Otani said.HMSI registrations have been averaging 10-15% growth over the previous year, he said. The company expects sales during the September-November festive period to exceed 1.9 million units, compared with over 1.8 million units in the corresponding period last year.

clusters.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
clusters.description: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage
